skill.name: managing-commits
skill.description: Helps write, validate, and organize conventional Git commits. It can analyze staged changes, review commit history, group files, and suggest GitHub issue references.
skill.summary: Create, validate, and organize conventional commits with GitHub issue context.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, commit template text, or subprocess calls that use explicit argv lists without shell execution. The only confirmed issue is the predictable temporary commit-message file used by the interactive commit helper. No prompt injection attempt or malicious exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Replace /tmp/commit-msg.txt with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile or mkstemp using restrictive permissions, then delete it after git commit completes.

remediation.issue: GitHub issue data is cached locally
remediation.suggestion: Document that issue titles, labels, URLs, and body previews may be stored under .claude/github-workflows, and offer a clear cache cleanup step.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts execute local git and gh commands
remediation.suggestion: Keep all command invocations shell-free, use explicit argument lists, and ask for user confirmation before commit or sync actions.

content.user_title: Improve Git Commits With Issue Context
content.value_statement: Poor commit messages make review and release automation harder. This skill helps create, validate, group, and link conventional commits to GitHub issues.
actual_capabilities: Generate conventional commit messages from staged Git changes.
Validate commit messages for type, scope, length, and clarity.
Review recent commit history for quality, size, and fixup opportunities.
Group changed files by scope and type for logical commit planning.
Suggest GitHub issue references from branch names and cached issue data.
limitations: It depends on local Git state and cannot infer unstaged intent without context.
GitHub issue suggestions require the GitHub CLI and an authenticated account.
Generated commit messages still need user review before committing.
History cleanup plans may require manual rebase decisions.

use_cases.title: Create Clean Feature Commits
use_cases.description: Turn staged work into a clear conventional commit with type, scope, body, and issue footer.

use_cases.title: Review Branch History
use_cases.description: Find weak messages, large commits, and fixup candidates before opening or merging a pull request.

use_cases.title: Connect Commits to GitHub Issues
use_cases.description: Use branch names, file paths, and cached issues to choose accurate Closes or Refs footers.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Commit Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my staged changes and suggest a conventional commit message. Include type, scope, subject, body, and issue footer when relevant.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one commit message.

prompt_templates.title: Validate My Last Commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my last commit message against conventional commit rules. Explain each issue and provide a clearer replacement.
prompt_templates.scenario: Quality check for an existing commit.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Logical Commits
prompt_templates.prompt: Review all changed files and group them into logical conventional commits. Show the files, proposed order, and issue references.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for multiple related changes.

prompt_templates.title: Clean Branch History
prompt_templates.prompt: Review commits on my current branch against main. Identify weak messages, large commits, fixups, and a safe cleanup plan.

output_examples.input: I staged authentication changes and need a commit message.
output_examples.output: A suggested conventional commit with an auth scope, a concise subject, a short rationale, and a relevant issue footer.

output_examples.input: Review the commits on this branch before I open a pull request.
output_examples.output: A commit quality report that separates valid commits, weak messages, oversized commits, and suggested cleanup actions.

output_examples.input: I changed API, tests, and documentation. Help me split the commits.
output_examples.output: A grouped commit plan with proposed types, scopes, file lists, order, and issue reference suggestions.

best_practices: Review staged files before accepting any generated commit message.
Keep one logical change per commit and split unrelated work.
Use issue footers only when the commit truly resolves or relates to that issue.
anti_patterns: Creating broad commits that mix features, fixes, tests, and documentation.
Using vague subjects such as update, stuff, changes, or final fix.
Adding Closes footers when the commit only partially relates to an issue.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps generate, validate, group, and review Git commits using conventional commit rules.

faq.question: Does it create commits automatically?
faq.answer: It can support commit workflows, but generated messages and commit actions should be reviewed before execution.

faq.question: Does it require the GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: GitHub issue integration requires the GitHub CLI. Basic commit message help can work with local Git context.

faq.question: Can it use private GitHub issue data?
faq.answer: It can sync issues visible to the authenticated GitHub CLI account and store a local project cache.

faq.question: Does it enforce conventional commits?
faq.answer: It validates and suggests messages. Repository hooks or CI checks are still needed for enforcement.

faq.question: Which AI tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
